title: The Ventriloquist's Illusion
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Kogoro, Ran, Conan, Inspector Megure, Officer Takagi) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old lower-fidelity case file correctly identified Riichi Tengan as the murderer and Kazuko/Togawa as victim/framed suspect -- confirmed against the full transcript. Two corrections made to the old file's object modeling: (1) the old file's 'stolen speakers and recorder' and 'bloodstained glasses' were described as merely 'planted,' but the transcript shows Tengan actively stole both from Togawa about a week beforehand specifically to engineer the frame -- modeled here with explicit `steals` edges. (2) The old file's o4 ('bloodstained gloves, hidden inside his ventriloquist doll') is not quite what the transcript shows: Tengan destroyed the real gloves after his acquittal, and the gloves Officer Takagi produces during the final confrontation are explicitly called fake by Kogoro (a bluff to provoke a reaction) -- the real physical evidence that breaks the case is faint trace fiber/blood/sweat-DNA left inside the doll itself, which the old file's clue descriptions (c1, c2) actually already captured correctly even though its object list did not. Modeled here as a single `doll` object carrying that trace evidence, rather than a separate 'gloves' object. case_type: murder.

attrs.title: recent winner of a long-sought international ventriloquism tournament
attrs.feigned_disorder: faked dissociative identity disorder, using his own doll voice, to build an insanity defense before the murder

attrs.staged_position: moved to the front before the murder
attrs.significance: Tengan's prize from his long-sought international tournament win; only his fingerprints found on it
attrs.staging_flaw: dust outline on the sideboard didn't match its new position

attrs.trick: wireless speakers hidden in the condo, recorder set on a timer to auto-play 'partner' voice lines and simulate possession
attrs.stolen_from: Togawa, about a week before the murder
attrs.found_at: set up inside Tengan's own condo living room

attrs.condition: splattered with the victim's blood, hidden under the lining of Togawa's bag
attrs.trace: a thread fiber caught on the hinge between the temple and the frame, later matched to a glove

attrs.trace_evidence: faint fiber matching the glasses' thread, the victim's blood, and sweat DNA (not Togawa's) all found inside
attrs.significance: Tengan's decades-long stage partner, present since his international tournament win; the one thing he never thought to destroy

clues.desc: Dust outline on the sideboard doesn't match the trophy's actual position in crime-scene photos -- it was moved there deliberately before the murder, proving premeditation rather than a spontaneous grab of whatever weapon was nearby.

The glove-thread fiber snagged on Togawa's glasses matches a fiber found inside Tengan's doll, and the sweat DNA on that fiber isn't Togawa's -- proving Tengan, not Togawa, wore the gloves that planted the glasses.

edges.motive_type: wounded pride over his wife's affair with his own apprentice
red herring: police theorized he wanted to silence his lover to protect his career

edges.method: bludgeoned with the trophy while she sat with her back turned
